review: Phase B close-out - security findings hand review (Part 1, item 1)
method: Every finding's cited evidence was re-derived from the APK itself and compared against what the detector reported. Verification used: `unzip -l` / extraction of the APK, ManifestInspector output, DEXInspector api_references / strings / class inventory, and the SecurityEvidenceIndex the rule engine actually evaluates. A finding is TRUE_POSITIVE only where the cited evidence was independently reproduced AND supports the claim the finding makes; FALSE_POSITIVE where the artifact exists but does not support the claim (or the matched artifact is not what was cited); UNCLEAR where the evidence is partly unsubstantiated.
scope_note: No rule severity, confidence, scoring, or detection threshold was changed by this review. Proposed changes are recorded in proposed_rule_changes and were NOT implemented.

findings.title: Accessibility Service Implementation
findings.explanation: PCAPdroid declares no AccessibilityService. The rule's probe matched only the read-only metadata class android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityServiceInfo (used to enumerate accessibility services installed on the device), via substring matching.
findings.independent_verification: ManifestInspector: services == [VpnReconnectService, CaptureService]; no component bound with BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE. Index APIs matching the probe: only 'android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityServiceInfo' and '...AccessibilityServiceInfo;->getSettingsActivityName()Ljava.lang.String'.

findings.title: Android Accessibility Service Implementation
findings.explanation: Same root cause as SEC-SPY-ACCESSIBILITY-001: fired on the API path with no implemented accessibility service present. (For AppManager the same rule fired on a genuine manifest service, so the rule has one sound evidence path and one unsound one.)
findings.independent_verification: Same verification as SEC-SPY-ACCESSIBILITY-001.

findings.title: Hardware & Persistent Device Identifier Collection Capability
findings.explanation: One of two cited evidence items is substantiated: the string 'android_id' is genuinely present. The second, 'Build.SERIAL', does not exist in the evidence index; only the bare token 'SERIAL' does, so that evidence line is the probe label rather than a matched artifact. The capability is plausible for a per-device VPN configuration but is not established by the evidence as cited.
findings.independent_verification: Index strings: 'android_id' present == True; any string equal to 'Build.SERIAL' == False; strings containing 'SERIAL' == ['SERIAL'].

findings.title: Device Boot Persistence Mechanism Detected
findings.explanation: RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED is genuinely declared. Benign by design: PCAPdroid restores its VPN capture service after reboot.
findings.independent_verification: ManifestInspector: 'android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED' in declared permissions == True.

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP URL References Detected
findings.explanation: At least one genuine cleartext URL is present ('http://t.me/PCAPdroid', the project's Telegram link). Precision caveat: the other cited items are XMPP protocol namespace URIs from libndpi.so ('http://jabber.org/protocol/...'), which are XML identifiers rather than network endpoints.
findings.independent_verification: DEX strings contain 'http://t.me/PCAPdroid' == True; remaining cited items are jabber.org/etherx.jabber.org namespace URIs inside lib/arm64-v8a/libndpi.so.

findings.title: Background Clipboard Access Capability

findings.independent_verification: DEX API references include 'android.content.ClipboardManager;->getPrimaryClip()Landroid.content.ClipData' and 'com.emanuelef.remote_capture.Utils;->copyToClipboard(Landroid.content.Context'.

evidence_cited_by_detector.description: Potential hardcoded Generic Private Key Header observed (masked): ----*******************----
Potential hardcoded Generic Private Key Header observed (masked): ----***********************----
Potential hardcoded Generic Private Key Header observed (masked): ----***********************----

findings.explanation: The PEM armor header string is present, but it is a parser constant inside the bundled BouncyCastle provider, not an embedded key. No key body accompanies it.
findings.independent_verification: DEX strings contain '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----' == True; 6,139 org.bouncycastle.* classes are bundled (incl. findings.title: Insecure or Broken Cryptographic Cipher Mode
findings.explanation: The cited DES strings come from the bundled BouncyCastle algorithm registry, not from an application cipher choice. A general-purpose provider necessarily names every algorithm it implements.
findings.independent_verification: DEX strings 'DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding' and 'DESede' present == True; bundled implementation classes verified: org.bouncycastle.crypto.engines.DESEngine, DESedeEngine, DESedeWrapEngine, generators.DESedeKeyGenerator, params.DESedeParameters.

PRC-01.title: Accessibility-service detection must require an implemented service, not a substring match
PRC-01.problem: `android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService` is matched as a substring, so it also matches `android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityServiceInfo` -- the read-only metadata class used to *enumerate* accessibility services installed on the device. An app that merely lists other apps' accessibility services is flagged as implementing one.
PRC-01.proposal: Require either (a) a manifest <service> bound with BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, or (b) an exact class reference to android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService, before firing.

PRC-02.title: Evidence should cite the matched artifact, not the rule's probe pattern
PRC-02.problem: Several findings print the rule's configured probe string as the evidence snippet rather than the artifact that actually matched. Example: PCAPdroid's device-identifier finding cites `Build.SERIAL`, but the only matching string in the APK is the bare token `SERIAL`; AppManager's accessibility finding cites `...AccessibilityService` while the matched artifact is `...AccessibilityServiceInfo`. This makes evidence non-traceable to the APK.
PRC-02.proposal: Record the matched artifact value (and its source: api/string/method/manifest) in Evidence.snippet.

PRC-03.title: Cleartext-URL detection must exclude XML namespace and parser-feature URIs
PRC-03.problem: `http://xmlpull.org/v1/doc/features.html#...`, `http://apache.org/xml/features/...`, `http://xml.org/sax/features/...`, `http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android` and XMPP protocol namespaces are API constant identifiers that are never dereferenced over the network. For AppManager, every cited 'cleartext URL' is of this kind.
PRC-03.proposal: Maintain an allowlist of well-known namespace/feature URI hosts and exclude them, or require the URL to co-occur with an HTTP client API reference.

PRC-04.title: Deduplicate overlapping rule pairs that report the same underlying fact
PRC-04.problem: Pairs of rules fire on one fact: SEC-VULN-BACKUP-001 + SEC-VULN-MANIFEST-BACKUP (allowBackup), SEC-MAL-CODE-EXEC + SEC-MAL-EXEC-001 (ProcessBuilder), SEC-MAL-DYN-LOAD + SEC-MAL-DYNLOAD-001 (PathClassLoader), SEC-VULN-CRYPTO-WEAK-CIPHER + SEC-VULN-WEAK-CIPHER-001, SEC-VULN-CRYPTO-WEAK-HASH + SEC-VULN-WEAK-HASH-001. This inflates finding counts.
PRC-04.proposal: Merge each pair, or mark one of each pair as a sub-finding of the other.

PRC-05.title: Nested-APK payload detection must check whether the nested APK contains code
PRC-05.problem: AppManager's 14 `frameworks/android/android-NN.apk` entries are flagged HIGH severity as `payload`. Each one was extracted and verified to contain only resources.arsc + AndroidManifest.xml -- zero DEX, zero native code. They are Android framework resource tables used to resolve other apps' resource IDs per API level, and cannot execute.
PRC-05.proposal: Inspect the nested archive: only classify as `payload` when it contains classes*.dex or a native library; otherwise report as an informational embedded-resource observation.

PRC-06.title: Aggregate per-file findings instead of emitting one finding per file
PRC-06.problem: 14 separate HIGH findings (one per embedded framework APK) and 7 separate entropy findings dominate AppManager's result set: 21 of 45 findings describe two phenomena.
PRC-06.proposal: Emit one finding per phenomenon with the file list as evidence items.

PRC-07.title: Hardcoded-secret detection must require key material, not just PEM armor
PRC-07.problem: `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` is present in AppManager, but it is the PEM parser constant shipped inside the bundled BouncyCastle provider (6,139 org.bouncycastle.* classes verified). No key body accompanies it.
PRC-07.proposal: Require a base64 key body following the armor header before reporting a secret.

PRC-08.title: Crypto-weakness findings must attribute the algorithm string to its owning package
PRC-08.problem: `DES/CBC/PKCS5Padding`, `DESede`, `Blowfish`, `SHA1`/`SHA-1` in AppManager all originate from the bundled BouncyCastle provider's algorithm registry (org.bouncycastle.crypto.engines.DESEngine / DESedeEngine / DESedeWrapEngine verified present). A general-purpose crypto provider necessarily names every algorithm it supports; this is not evidence that the application selects a weak cipher. SHA-1 additionally appears legitimately for v1 JAR signature verification, which AppManager performs.
PRC-08.proposal: Attribute the matched string to the declaring class/package and suppress (or downgrade to informational) when it belongs to a known crypto provider rather than application code.

PRC-09.title: Entropy findings should account for inherently-compressed file formats
PRC-09.problem: assets/blanks/blank.{odp,odt,pdf,pptx} and assets/dexopt/baseline.prof are flagged as high-entropy `payload`. ODF/OOXML are ZIP containers and PDF/baseline profiles are compressed, so high entropy is expected and carries no signal.
PRC-09.proposal: Treat known-compressed extensions as informational unless paired with a loader reference.

PRC-10.title: Domain extraction must reject package-name-shaped tokens and namespace hosts
PRC-10.problem: AppManager's SEC-NET-CAPABILITY-FLOW cites `androidx.core.app` and `io.github.muntashirakon.io` as 'external domain endpoints'. These are Java package names whose final segment collides with a real TLD (.app, .io). `schemas.android.com` is an XML namespace host, not a contacted endpoint.
PRC-10.proposal: Exclude tokens that match a declared application/library package prefix, and namespace hosts, from the domain set used by network-flow rules.

PRC-11.title: Device-identifier pattern list contains a non-identifier entry
PRC-11.problem: AppManager's SEC-SPY-DEVICE-IDENTIFIERS cites `getDeviceIdleController` as a 'telephony hardware identifier method reference'. DeviceIdleController is the doze/power-management service and is unrelated to device identity; it matches only because of the `getDeviceId` substring.
PRC-11.proposal: Anchor identifier patterns (word boundary / exact method name) to exclude getDeviceIdleController.

PRC-12.title: Exported-receiver finding should note the AppWidgetProvider exemption as context
PRC-12.problem: AppManager's 4 exported unprotected receivers were all verified to be app-widget providers (ClearCacheAppWidget, RecordingWidgetProvider, DataUsageAppWidget, ScreenTimeAppWidget). An AppWidgetProvider must be exported to receive launcher broadcasts.
PRC-12.proposal: Keep the finding (the exposure is real) but add context when the receiver's intent filter is APPWIDGET_UPDATE, rather than suppressing it.
